headline: Materials Lead, Semis Lag as Geopolitical Tension Colors Friday's Close
body_html:
Equities are holding a narrow positive tilt through midday Friday, with advancing issues edging decliners 291 to 254 across our 549-name universe. The tone is cautious rather than exuberant: gains are concentrated in defensive and commodity-linked pockets while growth-oriented technology faces consistent selling pressure. Materials sit at the top of the sector ledger, up 1.5%, followed by Homebuilders at 1.14% and Consumer at 0.83%, a rotation that suggests investors are gravitating toward tangible-asset exposure amid unresolved conflict in the Gulf region.

The standout mover of the session is Solstice Advanced Materials, surging 18.05% to claim the day's top spot among gainers. Gap Inc. is not far behind, posting a 16.73% advance that ranks among the sharpest retailer rallies seen this year. N-able adds 9.23%, lending a bright note to an otherwise pressured software complex. On the downside, semiconductors are absorbing the heaviest damage: Marvell Technology off 5.64% and the broader Semiconductors sector down 0.64% lead losses, with cybersecurity names CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks each shedding more than 3.9%.

Into the close, traders will watch whether the materials and homebuilder bid can hold as oil headlines continue to ripple through commodity desks. Any fresh signal from Strait of Hormuz negotiations could quickly reprice energy and transport names in either direction before the weekend.

briefs.headline: Solstice Advanced Materials Rockets Higher in Midday Trade
briefs.body: Specialty-chemicals name Solstice Advanced Materials is the session's most dramatic mover, up 18.05% as of midday. The surge lifts the broader Materials sector to the top of Friday's leaderboard. No corporate announcement has been publicly confirmed, but the move is drawing significant volume attention on trading desks.

briefs.headline: Gap Stages Double-Digit Rally, Brightening Consumer-Apparel Picture
briefs.body: Gap Inc. has climbed 16.73% on the session, offering a sharp counterpoint to the mixed consumer backdrop. The advance pushes the Consumer sector to a 0.83% gain overall. Traders are monitoring whether the move reflects genuine fundamental momentum or a short-covering event heading into the weekend.

briefs.headline: Strait of Hormuz Talks Stall as Oil Holds Near Weekly Lows
briefs.body: Crude prices are on track for a weekly decline as negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain deadlocked, with Iran's top security official publicly outlining conditions for any restart of maritime traffic. Gulf infrastructure spending is nonetheless accelerating, according to industry reports, as pipelines and port operators position for a prolonged disruption.

briefs.headline: Cybersecurity Names Retreat Sharply in Afternoon Selling
briefs.body: CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks are each falling more than 3.9% in Friday's session, compounding a rough stretch for the cybersecurity group. The selloff coincides with broader pressure on software and semiconductor names, suggesting a risk-off rotation out of high-multiple technology into more defensive corners of the market.

briefs.headline: BitGo Moves to Absorb NYDIG's Institutional Crypto Trading Arm
briefs.body: Digital-asset custodian BitGo has agreed to acquire the institutional trading business of NYDIG, a deal that signals renewed confidence in crypto market infrastructure as trading volumes rebound. The transaction is seen as a consolidation play, positioning BitGo to capture a larger share of growing institutional order flow in digital assets.

briefs.headline: G20 Finance Gathering to Fold Iran Sanctions Into Growth Agenda
briefs.body: A U.S.-hosted G20 finance ministers meeting is set to address Iran sanctions alongside broader discussions on global growth and economic imbalances, according to a senior Treasury official. The inclusion of sanctions on a multilateral finance agenda underscores how deeply the Gulf conflict has become entangled with the international economic policy calendar.
